content.value_statement: Manual raffle selection can look biased and is hard to document. This skill guides fair random draws from lists, files, or Google Sheets.
actual_capabilities: Selects one or more random winners from plain lists, CSV files, Excel files, or Google Sheets.
Supports exclusions so previous winners or ineligible entries can be skipped.
Can pick runner-ups after the main winner selection.
Supports weighted selection when an entries column represents ticket counts.
Shows winner details, selection method, and timestamp for audit records.
Provides workflows for giveaways, event raffles, and random team assignments.
limitations: It is an instruction-only skill and does not include its own executable raffle engine.
Google Sheets and local file access depend on the host tool permissions.
Fair results depend on clean participant data and clear eligibility rules.
It does not verify legal contest requirements or participant consent.

use_cases.title: Run a subscriber giveaway
use_cases.description: Pick a winner from a newsletter, Slack, or Google Form export and record the draw details.

use_cases.title: Draw event raffle prizes
use_cases.description: Select several winners and runner-ups from an attendee CSV while avoiding duplicate winners.

use_cases.title: Assign participants randomly
use_cases.description: Split a participant list into fair groups for surveys, tests, workshops, or team activities.

prompt_templates.title: Pick one winner from a list
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick one random winner from this list. Show the selected name, selection method, and timestamp: [paste entries].

prompt_templates.title: Pick winners from a file
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick three random winners from [file name]. Exclude duplicate people and show the row number for each winner.

prompt_templates.title: Pick winner and runner-ups
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick one winner and three runner-ups from [source]. Exclude these previous winners: [names]. Include a clear audit summary.

prompt_templates.title: Run a weighted raffle
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the entries column as ticket weight and pick [number] winners from [source]. Explain how weights affected the draw.

output_examples.input: Pick one random winner from a Google Sheet with 247 entries.
output_examples.output: Winner selected: Sarah Johnson from row 142. Selection method: cryptographically random. Timestamp recorded for verification.

output_examples.input: Pick one winner and three runner-ups from attendees.csv, excluding previous winners.
output_examples.output: Winner and runner-ups selected with duplicate checks applied. The result includes row references, excluded names, and an audit note.

best_practices: Clean the entry list before drawing winners, including duplicate and ineligible entries.
Save the timestamp, source file name, and selection method for transparency.
Pick runner-ups when prizes require eligibility checks or winner confirmation.
anti_patterns: Do not change the entry list after seeing the selected winner.
Do not publish personal data that is not needed for the announcement.
Do not rely on weighted draws unless the ticket count column is verified.

faq.question: Can it pick winners from Google Sheets?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide winner selection from a Google Sheet when the host tool can access the sheet.

faq.question: Can it prevent duplicate winners?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports exclusions and duplicate prevention during multi-winner draws.

faq.question: Does it support weighted raffles?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use an entries column as the weight for ticket-based selection.

faq.question: Does it create a public audit trail?
faq.answer: It can include winner details, row references, selection method, and timestamp for records.

faq.question: Can it verify contest eligibility?
faq.answer: No. You must verify eligibility rules, legal requirements, and participant consent separately.

faq.question: Is it safe for private participant data?
faq.answer: Use the minimum required fields and avoid publishing emails or private identifiers unless consent allows it.
